Student prototype: one temperature-limited foil pixel*

Download Markdown ↓

Proposed student implementation; not reviewed by Yon Visell.

  • Build one foil-heater channel and end each fixed-voltage heating pulse from a resistance-assisted temperature estimate.
  • Track metal temperature T\mathsf{T}T and surrounding-material temperature S\mathsf{S}S; retain both between pulses.
  • Begin with pulses that the available pyrometer resolves and that produce useful tactile displacement or force.
  • Fit three thermal coefficients on one sequence, then check the fixed controller on a different sequence.
  • Deliver a working pulse controller and recorded electrical, temperature and tactile-output results.

1. Build one channel

Voltage and current measurements let the controller estimate foil temperature and end the heating pulse.

Use a Teensy 4.1, INA253EVM A3 current sensor, CSD17305Q5A switch and adjustable 0–5 V supply with current below 5 A. Connect supply positive → approximately 1 Ω foil → current sensor → switch → supply negative. Use a copper carrier for the switch.

Attach separate voltage-sense wires at the foil pads. Each feeds a 1 kΩ/1 kΩ divider with 1 nF at its midpoint. The current output uses 100 Ω/1 nF. Connect the gate through 1 kΩ and add a 100 kΩ gate-to-source pull-down. Use 3.3 V sensor and controller signals. The pyrometer views the active foil; its spot must fit the target.

2. Measure the inputs

Calibration lets the controller distinguish a temperature rise from electrical measurement error.

  1. Electrical conversion: use two known values per voltage/current channel, then check an intermediate value. For ADC code n\mathsf{n}n, store x=an+b\mathsf{x=an+b}x=an+b, with a=(x2−x1)/(n2−n1)\mathsf{a=(x_2-x_1)/(n_2-n_1)}a=(x2​−x1​)/(n2​−n1​), b=x1−an1\mathsf{b=x_1-an_1}b=x1​−an1​. Calibrate sensor-branch current. Reconstruct heater quantities as V=V+−V−\mathsf{V=V_+-V_-}V=V+​−V−​, I=Is+V−/2000\mathsf{I=I_s+V_-/2000}I=Is​+V−​/2000 after settling.
  2. Timing and power: pulse a stable resistor. Record settling time, maximum heater power Pmax⁡\mathsf{P_{\max}}Pmax​, turn-off delay and residual OFF power. Check the complete voltage/current sample cycle.
  3. Temperature curve: at settled temperature references, record resistance and pyrometer temperature. Include the intended working range and any resistance turning point. Use q(T)=R(T)/R0\mathsf{q(T)=R(T)/R_0}q(T)=R(T)/R0​, where R0\mathsf{R_0}R0​ is measured at ambient A\mathsf{A}A. Normalize a previously measured stock curve by its value at A\mathsf{A}A. Apply emissivity correction and compare center/end temperatures across the active foil; use a sufficiently uniform specimen for the material curve.
  4. Heat capacity: calculate active foil mass times alloy specific heat, C(T)=mcp(T)\mathsf{C(T)=mc_p(T)}C(T)=mcp​(T). Store its minimum Cmin⁡\mathsf{C_{\min}}Cmin​.
  5. Useful pulse: choose one fixed voltage and finite duration that give the desired tactile response within the independently observed temperature range. The pyrometer must resolve that pulse; check its response time and recorded trace before using it as a dynamic reference.

To estimate resistance between measured temperatures, join neighboring calibration points with a straight line:

q(U)=qj+(qj+1−qj)(U−Tj)/(Tj+1−Tj).\mathsf{q(U)=q_j+(q_{j+1}-q_j)(U-T_j)/(T_{j+1}-T_j).}q(U)=qj​+(qj+1​−qj​)(U−Tj​)/(Tj+1​−Tj​).

Precompute q(U)\mathsf{q(U)}q(U) at 1 °C spacing and the largest absolute segment slope L\mathsf{L}L. The spacing sets numerical resolution. Record normalized-resistance error eR>0\mathsf{e_R>0}eR​>0 from electrical checks and curve uncertainty.

3. Fit and set the stopping allowance

Fit heat loss and retention, then measure the temperature allowance needed for switch-off.

Use fixed voltage, pulse width tp\mathsf{t_p}tp​ and start-to-start interval tr>tp\mathsf{t_r>t_p}tr​>tp​. Record this fitting sequence:

  1. From ambient, apply one pulse; wait 4tr\mathsf{4t_r}4tr​ after turn-off.
  2. Apply four pulses starting every tr\mathsf{t_r}tr​.
  3. Wait tr\mathsf{t_r}tr​ after the final turn-off; apply one pulse.
  4. Wait 4tr\mathsf{4t_r}4tr​ after turn-off; apply one pulse.

Here G\mathsf{G}G controls heat leaving the foil, β\mathsf{\beta}β controls warming of the surroundings, and γ\mathsf{\gamma}γ controls their cooling toward ambient. Fit positive values by replaying

Tnew=T+Δt[P−G(T−S)]/C(T),Snew=S+Δt[β(T−S)−γ(S−A)]\mathsf{T_{\rm new}=T+\Delta t[P-G(T-S)]/C(T),\qquad S_{\rm new}=S+\Delta t[\beta(T-S)-\gamma(S-A)]}Tnew​=T+Δt[P−G(T−S)]/C(T),Snew​=S+Δt[β(T−S)−γ(S−A)]

and minimizing ∑[q(T)−V/(IR0)]2\mathsf{\sum[q(T)-V/(IR_0)]^2}∑[q(T)−V/(IR0​)]2. Use measured power during settled conduction, Pmax⁡\mathsf{P_{\max}}Pmax​ during settling and measured OFF power. Keep both temperatures through every pause. During fitting, omit resistance correction so it cannot conceal errors in the thermal prediction. A direct multiplicative search over the three coefficients is sufficient for the initial fit.

Set search width w≥1\mathsf{w\ge1}w≥1 K from the largest uncorrected-model temperature error on this record, adding reference uncertainty and one grid step. Replay the resistance-corrected observer below. Set stopping allowance M\mathsf{M}M from its largest temperature underestimation, plus reference uncertainty and one grid step. Freeze these values before the separate check.

4. Run the local controller

Each update predicts heating, corrects it using resistance and sets the switch-off deadline.

Initialize T=S=A\mathsf{T=S=A}T=S=A after cooling. Before a pulse, update the stored cooling state, fix its original end time and initialize the first-reading expiry. In one uninterrupted operation, check the deadline, arm the timer and enable the switch if the deadline is future. Use a clock step Δt≤0.1min⁡(Cmin⁡/G,1/(β+γ))\mathsf{\Delta t\le0.1\min(C_{\min}/G,1/(\beta+\gamma))}Δt≤0.1min(Cmin​/G,1/(β+γ)); divide longer gaps into such steps. Each update receives aligned voltage/current and its timestamp. Here Tc\mathsf{T_c}Tc​ is the temperature ceiling; data_age is the maximum permitted interval between valid readings. An invalid reading has timed out, saturated, or fallen below the calibrated current range.

At each clock update:
    if timestamp is stale or settled readings are invalid: switch OFF; return
    dt = sample_time-state_time
    P = average of previous and current V*I during settled conduction
    use Pmax during settling; use measured OFF power while off
    remaining = dt
    while remaining > 0:
        h = min(remaining,0.1*min(Cmin/G,1/(beta+gamma)))
        Tnew = T + h*(P-G*(T-S))/C(T)
        Snew = S + h*(beta*(T-S)-gamma*(S-A))
        T = Tnew; S = Snew; state_time = state_time+h
        remaining = remaining-h
        if T is outside calibration: switch OFF; return
    if switch is OFF: retain T,S; return
    if reading is settled:
        y = V/(I*R0); predicted = T
        runs = 0; previous_pass = false; best_cost = infinity
        for consecutive grid temperatures U within predicted ± w:
            passes = abs(y-q[U]) <= eR + L*grid_step
            if passes and not previous_pass: runs = runs+1
            if passes:
                cost = ((U-predicted)/w)^2 + ((y-q[U])/eR)^2
                if cost < best_cost: best_cost = cost; best_T = U
            previous_pass = passes
        if runs != 1: switch OFF; return ambiguity_or_mismatch
        q_pred = interpolate_q(predicted)
        if abs(y-q_pred) <= eR + L*grid_step:
            if ((y-q_pred)/eR)^2 <= best_cost: best_T = predicted
        T = best_T; last_valid_time = sample_time
    thermal_end = state_time + (Tc-M-max(T,S))*Cmin/Pmax - off_delay
    deadline = min(thermal_end,original_end,last_valid_time+data_age-off_delay)
    if deadline <= now: switch OFF
    else: arm local timer for deadline

The score favors temperatures close to both the prediction and the measured resistance. Multiple separated compatible runs stop the pulse. Including the continuous prediction preserves small temperature rises where resistance provides little temperature information. Faults disable further pulses until resolved; reset requires the established cooldown.

5. Check the result independently

A different pulse sequence checks temperature-limited heating and useful tactile output with the completed controller.

Keep coefficients and allowances fixed:

  1. From ambient, apply four pulses of widths tp/2,tp,tp/2,tp\mathsf{t_p/2,t_p,t_p/2,t_p}tp​/2,tp​,tp​/2,tp​, with starts separated by tr\mathsf{t_r}tr​.
  2. Wait 2tr\mathsf{2t_r}2tr​ after the last turn-off; apply one pulse of width tp\mathsf{t_p}tp​.
  3. Use full-width pulses throughout if a half pulse supplies no settled reading.
  4. Record resistance, pyrometer temperature, estimated temperature, gate transitions and tactile output. Confirm that pulses end before the independently observed temperature exceeds the selected ceiling and that the chosen tactile response is useful and repeatable.

This check establishes the tested pulse and load range. The estimate represents effective foil temperature; spatial hotspots and pulses faster than the reference instrument require different temperature evidence.

Appendix: subsequent improvements

Use the first result to choose the next improvement: faster pulses that the temperature reference can resolve, better electrical precision if resistance error dominates, or additional channels. Check each change against the same temperature and tactile-output goals.
